findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut.
findings.body: The grant shortcut is the last two characters of the 6-character prefix, at indexes 4 to 6. `substring(3, 5)` reads the last character of the token type and the first of the grant (for `onrtac` it returns "ta"), so it never equals a 2-letter grant shortcut. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the values match. As a result every event assertion that uses this matcher passes whatever grant type is encoded, and a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match. Fix: check the length is 6 and use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup.
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to the SPI as an abstract method with no default. Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations then fail to compile. Already-built jars throw AbstractMethodError in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`. A factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw NPE. In every case Keycloak fails to start. Add a default implementation, for example one that derives a shortcut or returns null, and handle a null shortcut in postInit by mapping it to the unknown value.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId tests grantType instead.
findings.body: This line repeats the `grantType` check under the rawTokenId message, so `rawTokenId` is never null-checked. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then produces a token id like `onrtac:null`. Check `rawTokenId` instead.

held.title: The public Context copy constructor was removed without any need from this feature.
held.body: The hunk deletes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor. Nothing in the request requires removing it, and it is public SPI API: any caller that copies a Context (core code not shown here or custom grant/token-exchange extensions) will no longer compile. If it is kept, it should also copy the new `grantType` field. I could not see whether core code still calls it.
